archive.shelfmark_note: Page titles in the HRC records are archival shelfmarks: MSS_WildeO_2_7_002 is Oscar Wilde Papers, Box 2, Folder 7, image 002.
archive.page_id_note: The archival shelfmark, MSS_WildeO_<box>_<folder>_<image>. `pointer` is a CONTENTdm id, which a change of platform would break.

purpose: Page scans of the digitized Wilde correspondence, for verifying that emphasis (underlines) in the original letters is preserved in web/data quote markup.

rights_note.note: Per-page metadata in the HRC CONTENTdm records carries the RightsStatements.org marker. Page-level titles are the archival shelfmarks (e.g. MSS_WildeO_2_7_002 = Oscar Wilde Papers, Box 2, Folder 7, image 002).

notes: Per-page `file` is relative to `../../manuscripts/<key>/`, the private tree that holds the images. The path is metadata; the images are what stays unpublished.

Our `page` is the Ransom Center's own image number, not a count of our own: their compound object labels its fourth child 'Image 4', that child's title is the shelfmark MSS_WildeO_2_10_004, and the shelfmark suffix equals our `page` for all 572 pages here. Checked against the CONTENTdm item API on 2026-08-11. That is why `letter_id` here IS the shelfmark - hrc/MSS_WildeO_2_10_004, not hrc/2777#4 - since `itemId` is a CONTENTdm pointer that a change of platform would break, and a reading room wants Box 2, Folder 10 rather than 2777. `itemId` and `page` stay as the local pointer into our own image tree, which is a different job from identity.

13 of the collection's 23 items were downloaded: all correspondence items. The 10 literary-work/manuscript items (plays, poems, third-party works) were excluded; their itemIds are 3220, 1785, 2504, 2083, 2980, 3157, 2299, 1967, 2940, 3432.
Image files are full-resolution IIIF JPEGs (native size, ~2000px wide), one per manuscript page.

Items 2568 (Wilde to recipients A-Z), 2777/2854/2898 (letters to Wilde), and 3286/3305/3401/3411 (third-party) are grab-bag folders: page-level identification of the recipient/author requires reading each letter, which the verification AI is expected to do.

A `matches` entry carries only structured facts: `pages`, `what`, `printed` {work, locator} and, where there is no printed pointer, `person`. Prose about why an entry matters lives in this archive's README, not here - the manifest restates neither the connection nor the commentary.

Two letters the Complete Letters place at Texas are NOT among the 572 pages scanned here: p. 462, to an Unidentified Correspondent, 'Dear Sir, There is an error of setting in my article, which pray correct at once'; and p. 1111, a postcard to Leonard Smithers, 'This is to show you where the poet is now living. I sent you the proofs days ago'. Every image in all thirteen items has been identified, so they are not hiding in what we hold - the Ransom Center has Wilde material outside these thirteen items. Worth a request if either is ever quoted. Three letters here are apparently UNCOLLECTED - present in the archive and absent from the volume: 2568 image 13 to Arthur Humphreys, 2568 image 18 to Richard D'Oyly Carte (the volume prints no letter to Carte at all), and 2568 images 16-17 to an unidentified 'My dear Doctor'. The first two were checked against every Humphreys and Carte heading in the volume; the third cannot be checked by heading because the addressee is unknown, so it is recorded as not found rather than not printed.

Derived images are allowed in the private image tree but must be quarantined and labelled: a subfolder, never beside the archive's own files, so nothing globbing `page-*.jpg` mistakes them for archive pages and so the file tree alone shows what came from the institution and what we made. The only set so far is `hrc/3286-third-party-a-h/derived-positives/`, which exists because the originals are reversed negatives that cannot otherwise be read.

Wilde to John Boyle O'Reilly, [1882], The Pilot, Boston - on his mother's poems. Image 5 is a typed copy of the same letter
TYPED COPY of the letter to John Boyle O'Reilly whose autograph is images 2-4 of this item

Wilde to Ada Leverson, [circa 13 March 1895], Hotel Avondale - 'then return to fight with panthers'. Autograph. Images 32-33 are an identifying slip and a photographic reproduction of this same letter, not a second original
Two envelopes to Arthur Fish at Cassell & Co, Belle Sauvage Yard, with 16 Tite Street embossed on the flaps
TYPED COPY, not an autograph, of Wilde to Michael Davitt, [late May or early June 1897], marked 'Private and Confidential', on the flogging of prisoner A.2.11; the autograph is MS Dublin

Wilde to Arthur L. Humphreys, 16 Tite Street - 'I know of no cleverer person than yours, so I send you enclosed. Will you communicate with Mr Leader?' Signed in full, with the Ransom Center's red TxU stamp on the leaf and a pencil acquisition date 3/11/51. NOT IN THE COMPLETE LETTERS: the volume prints six letters to Humphreys (pp. 604, 611, 623, 630, and two later), and this is none of them. Apparently uncollected
Wilde to an Unidentified Correspondent ('My dear Edith'), [? 1891] - declining to join 'the chorus of your nightingales'

Wilde to an unidentified correspondent, 9 Charles Street, Grosvenor Square - 'My dear Doctor', accepting supper after a lecture, coming down by the 5.30 from St Pancras, and noting that the Club's formal invitation has not yet come, 'with you in the chair'. Lecture-tour period. NOT FOUND in the Complete Letters on two search passes; the addressee is unidentified, which makes it hard to search by heading, so this is 'not found' rather than 'not printed'

Wilde to Richard D'Oyly Carte, [early 1882], Arlington Hotel, Washington, written on J. M. Stoddart & Co, Publishers, Philadelphia paper - 'You see the unpleasant results of leaving me without a manager. Please don't let it occur again for both our sakes: Morse should be always with me', with 'both our sakes' underlined. NOT IN THE COMPLETE LETTERS, which print no letter to Carte at all. It belongs to the same episode as the letter to George Lewis of 9 February 1882 at p. 134 - 'Carte blundered in leaving me without a manager, and Forbes through the most foolish and mad jealousy tried to lure me into a newspaper correspondence' - so this is Wilde complaining to Carte directly on the same days he complained to his solicitor about Carte. Apparently uncollected
Wilde to Arthur Clifton, [January 1889], Woman's World - accepting his roundel for the March number
Wilde to Lawrence Barrett, [? July 1889], 16 Tite Street - on The Duchess of Padua
Wilde to George Bedborough, [? October 1898], Hotel de Nice - envelope, then the letter. Image 28, skipped, is a dealer's catalogue description of it
Dealer's catalogue clipping, lot 256, quoting a letter of March 1898 on the essays and the Ballad - context, not a manuscript
Photostat of the letter to Ada Leverson whose autograph is image 6, with a typed curatorial note on the Punch parody 'The Minx - A Poem in Prose'
Wilde to Frederick Locker, [1881], 13 Salisbury Street - Frank Miles's picture and 'Tea and Beauties'

Wilde to Gerald Maxwell, [? 1888] - envelope to the Post Office, Sidmouth, and the letter: 'You seem to have thrilled the great Bournemouth school of criticism.' Image 39 was catalogued separately at first and is a further leaf of this same letter
Wilde to Edwin Strachan Morgan, [1888], 16 Tite Street - returning his manuscript, 'wanting in reserve, balance, and sobriety'
Wilde to Charles Ricketts, [1889], 16 Tite Street - 'It is not a forgery at all; it is an authentic Clouet'
Wilde to Oscar Browning, [1888], Woman's World, La Belle Sauvage - 'pillage the Americans who are rich, and get your £40'
Envelope, D'Oyly Carte's Opera Comique Companies, to E. C. Stedman Esq - 1882 American tour
Wilde to Charlotte Riddell, [? 1887], 16 Tite Street - inviting her to contribute to a monthly magazine

TYPED EXTRACTS, not autographs, from Wilde's letters to Robert Ross, Paris, May to July 1898 - the Campbell's Bar scene with Robert Sherard, Bosie and Maurice Gilbert, and Frank Harris on the Greek passions of Christ and Shakespeare. Several letters, excerpted and separated by rules; the autographs are MS Clark
Wilde to Leonard Smithers, Tuesday [1898], Hotel d'Alsace - 'Would you, or could you, let me have four copies of my last play?'; 'four' underlined
Envelope to Leonard Smithers, Royal Arcade, Old Bond Street, 'Angleterre' underlined; Paris postmark, London DE 2 98 on the verso - belongs with images 50-51

Wilde to Leonard Smithers, [1899], Taverne Pousset, Paris - returning the proofs of The Importance of Being Earnest, on whether Chasuble and Prism carry their titles in the head-lines, and the Era announcement
Wilde to Leonard Smithers, Tuesday 19 October [1897], Hotel Royal des Etrangers, Naples - on an edition of 500, of which 100 to the press
Envelope to Leonard Smithers with a Hotel Royal, Naples label; Napoli Ferrovia 19 10 98 postmark, docketed on the verso 'Ballad of Reading Gaol' - belongs with images 56-57
Wilde to J. M. Stoddart, [1882] - asking for the reviews of Todd's poems
Wilde to Emily Thursfield, [1884], Raven Hotel, Shrewsbury - accepting an invitation
Presentation inscription, 'From your affectionate son the author, with his love' - a slip, not a letter

Parke-Bernet auction catalogue clipping, sale of 25 October 1960, lot 260, describing the sixteen-page pencil letter to Alexander that is images 1-12 of this item - context, not a manuscript
Wilde to George Alexander, [? mid-August 1894], 16 Tite Street - on giving Hare the refusal of his next play

items.title: Letters from Oscar Wilde to Frank Harris

matches.what: Wilde to Frank Harris, [postmark 13 August 1898], Hotel d'Alsace - on Harris's appreciation of Rodin's 'Balzac' and his Shakespeare essays; 'Paris is terrible in its heat'

Wilde to Frank Harris, 21 November 1900, Hotel d'Alsace - 'I have now been in bed for nearly ten weeks', demanding the money owed on Mr and Mrs Daventry. Written nine days before his death, and dictated: the body is in Maurice Gilbert's hand, the close in Wilde's own
Wilde to Frank Harris, [October 1900], Paris - 'Your telegram just arrived. I have no money to pay for telegrams'; the Daventry money dispute, on Smithers, Kyrle Bellew and the broken agreement
Wilde to Frank Harris, [1900] - 'According to our agreement you were to pay me 175 pounds within a week'; the Daventry money dispute
Envelope to Frank Harris, Melbury Lodge, Kingston Hill, Surrey, postmark OC 23 00

Telegram, Wilde to Frank Harris, Paris - 'If you come over tomorrow come and see me first. Nethersole very impossible'. Folio not yet confirmed at the page; the volume indexes Louis Nethersole at 1199
Wilde to Frank Harris, 26 September 1900, Elysee Palace Hotel - the signed assignment of the plot and scenario of 'Her Second Chance', carrying 27s.6d. of official-looking stamps
Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 19 March 1899], Gland, Canton Vaud - 'in Switzerland with Mellor: a rather dreadful combination'
Wilde to Frank Harris, Tuesday [18 September 1900], Hotel d'Alsace - 'if you only send a wire from Calais, I may miss it'; endorsed 'Received 19 September 1900'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [1900], Pavillon d'Armenonville, Bois de Boulogne
Wilde to Frank Harris, [late May 1899], on Taverne de l'Opera paper but headed Hotel Marsollier - Armand Point's address, and Mirbeau
Wilde to Frank Harris, [? March 1898], Hotel de Nice - 'The Saturday arrived last night, and I read your article on Shakespeare'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 15 March 1898], Hotel de Nice - on Symons's review of the Ballad in the Saturday Review
Wilde to Frank Harris, [? February 1899], Terminus Hotel, Nice - asking for the promised £20, 'otherwise I shall be in a very serious mess here'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [September 1900], Hotel d'Alsace - 'Since you left Paris I have not received, till this morning, a...'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [1900], Paris - 'Our misunderstanding of last night'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 26 July 1899], Hotel de l'Ecu, Chenneviers-sur-Marne - 'Please write to me under my real name here'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 23 February 1899], Hotel des Alpes-Maritimes, rue d'Angleterre, Nice - having left the Terminus, and the Arnold/Dowden bet with Mellor
Wilde to Frank Harris, Thursday [1899], Napoule - 'you are regarded at Napoule as the future regenerator of the spot'; Ribot's glass-walled oyster pavilions on the porphyry rocks
Wilde to Frank Harris, [? February 1899], Hotel Terminus, Nice - 'Many, many thanks for your enclosure and letter'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 22 February 1899], Hotel Terminus & Cosmopolitain, Monte Carlo - 'I am in great trouble'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [end February 1898], Hotel de Nice - 'une vraie poignee de main'. Image 66 is Harris's own printed leaf of the letter, not the manuscript
Wilde to Frank Harris, [? 13 June 1897], Berneval - fifteen sides, the sheets numbered by Wilde 1 to 5; the postscript about Lawley follows the signature
Wilde to Frank Harris, [? March 1898], Hotel de Nice - 'You have been so good and generous to me that I hate to'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [? 1892], Lyric Club - 'I have just come back from Homburg'
Envelope to Frank Harris, Melbury Lodge, Kingston, Surrey, annotated 'NO. II' and, on the verso, 'No. 2 about scenario'
Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 27 March 1899], Gland - on Georgette Leblanc and de Lara's Messaline

Wilde to George Ives, [September 1900], Paris - 'Many thanks: it is most kind of you'; letter and envelope
